title: 2009 AMC 12A Problem 24
statement: The tower function of twos is defined recursively as follows: \(T(1) = 2\) and \(T(n + 1) = 2^{T(n)}\) for \(n \ge 1.\) Let \(A = (T(2009))^{T(2009)}\) and \(B = (T(2009))^A.\) What is the largest integer \(k\) such that \[\underbrace{\log_2 \log_2 \log_2 \ldots \log_2}_{k} B\] is defined?

solutions.text:
Since \(\log_2 T(n + 1) = T(n),\) each application of \(\log_2\) strips one \(2\) off the top of a tower of twos.

Write \(T_j=T(j),\) and let \(L_j\) be the result of applying \(\log_2\) to \(B\) exactly \(j\) times. The first two results are \[ \begin{aligned} L_1 &= A\,T_{2008}, \\ L_2 &= T_{2009}T_{2008}+T_{2007}. \end{aligned} \]

For the lower bound, \[ \begin{aligned} L_3 &\gt \log_2(T_{2009}T_{2008}) \\ &= T_{2008}+T_{2007} \\ &\gt T_{2008}. \end{aligned} \] Repeatedly taking logarithms gives \(L_{k+3} \gt T_{2008-k}\) for \(0\le k\le 2007.\) In particular, \(L_{2010}\gt2,\) so \(L_{2011}\gt1\) and \(L_{2012}\gt0.\) Thus \(L_{2013}\) is defined.

For the upper bound, \(T_{2007}\lt T_{2008}T_{2009},\) so \[ \begin{aligned} L_3 &\lt 1+T_{2007}+T_{2008} \\ &\lt 2T_{2008}, \\ L_4 &\lt 1+T_{2007} \lt T_{2008}. \end{aligned} \] Repeating the last comparison gives \(L_{k+4}\lt T_{2008-k}\) for \(0\le k\le2007.\) Hence \(L_{2011}\lt2.\) Together with the lower bound, this yields \(0\lt L_{2012}\lt1,\) so \(L_{2013}\lt0.\) Therefore \(L_{2014}\) is undefined, and the largest possible \(k\) is \(2013.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Repeatedly applying \(\log_2\) peels one level off a tower: \(\log_2 T(n + 1) = T(n)\)
Track how many logs \(B = (T(2009))^A\) can survive before the value drops below \(1\)
